Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

rob verb

also rob someone of, be robbed, mug, mugging

classical

Cic. Verr. 2.4.37: Apollōnium omnī argentō spoliāstī (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 196

spoliō, spoliāre, spoliāvī, spoliātum

verb, first conjugation: aliquem aliquā rē spoliāre

rob, strip (someone of something)

Other words

  • rapiō, rapere, rapuī, raptum — seize, carry off by force

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 196

  • mulcō, mulcāre, mulcāvī, mulcātum — beat up, handle roughly; Traupman’s word for “mug”

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 1.2.9: ipsum dominum atque omnem familiam mulcāvit usque ad mortem (Lewis & Short); Traupman 348

    Classically mulcāre is to beat, cudgel, maltreat (Plautus, Cicero); it says nothing of robbing.

Examples

  • Istī latrōnēs macellārium omnī argentō ējus spoliāvērunt.

    Those robbers robbed the grocer of all his money.Traupman 191

See also robbery, steal, thief.

SourcesLewis & Short: spolio · Lewis & Short: rapio · Lewis & Short: mulco

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 191, 196.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
